subject: Polity
topic: Directive Principles of State Policy – Final 110% Set

mcqs.q: Consider the following statements regarding the classification and nature of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP): 1. The Constitution of India explicitly categorizes the Directive Principles into three broad categories: Socialist, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual. 2. Though legally non-justiciable, Article 37 explicitly declares that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country. 3. It is the constitutional duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the additions made to the Directive Principles by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976: 1. It added the directive to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children (Article 39). 2. It added the directive to promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to the poor (Article 39A). 3. It added the directive to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities (Article 38). How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the legal supremacy battle between Fundamental Rights and DPSP (The Article 31C Trap): 1. Currently, all Directive Principles enjoy legal supremacy over the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Articles 14 and 19. 2. The 42nd Amendment Act attempted to give supremacy to all Directive Principles over Articles 14 and 19. 3. The Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills case (1980) held that the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Part III and Part IV. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the Directives contained outside Part IV of the Constitution: 1. The directive to provide instruction in the mother-tongue applies to linguistic minority groups at both the primary and secondary stages of education. 2. The directive to promote the spread of the Hindi language is located in Part XVII of the Constitution. 3. The claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to services and posts are mentioned in Part XVI of the Constitution. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding Article 31C, which was added by the 25th Amendment Act, 1971: 1. It protects any law seeking to implement the directives contained in Article 39(b) and (c) from being challenged on the ground of contravention of Article 14 or Article 19. 2. It originally contained a provision stating that if a law contains a declaration that it is for giving effect to such policy, it cannot be questioned in any court. 3. The Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case upheld the first provision of Article 31C but struck down the second provision regarding judicial review. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002: 1. It changed the subject-matter of Article 45 in the Directive Principles. 2. Prior to the amendment, Article 45 directed the state to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. 3. To complement this change, the amendment also added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the specific directives under Article 39: 1. Article 39(b) directs the state to secure that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good. 2. Article 39(c) directs the state to ensure that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth to the common detriment. 3. A law made to implement Article 39(b) and (c) can constitutionally override the Right to Equality (Article 14). How many of the above statements are correct?

Which of the following Directive Principles are strictly based on Gandhian ideology? 1. To promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operation basis in rural areas. 2. To prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs which are injurious to health. 3. To prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle. Select the correct answer:

Consider the following statements regarding the 44th and 97th Constitutional Amendment Acts: 1. The 44th Amendment Act added the directive to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities. 2. The 97th Amendment Act added the directive to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies. 3. Both of these newly added directives belong to the Socialist category of principles. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the historical roots of the Directive Principles: 1. They resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' enumerated in the Government of India Act of 1935. 2. The 'Instrument of Instructions' was issued to the Governor-General and Governors of the colonies by the British Government. 3. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explicitly stated that the Directive Principles are merely another name for the Instrument of Instructions. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the role of DPSP in Judicial Review: 1. Because they are non-justiciable, courts cannot use Directive Principles to determine the constitutional validity of any law. 2. The Supreme Court has ruled that a law seeking to give effect to a DPSP may be considered 'reasonable' in relation to restrictions under Article 14 or 19. 3. DPSP can be legally enforced by the High Courts under Article 226 if the State completely ignores them for a period exceeding ten years. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of the conflict between Fundamental Rights and DPSP: 1. In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that in case of conflict, Fundamental Rights would prevail over DPSP. 2. In the Golaknath case (1967), the Court ruled that Fundamental Rights could be amended by Parliament to give effect to Directive Principles. 3. The 24th Amendment Act was enacted by Parliament specifically to assert its power to abridge any Fundamental Right. How many of the above statements are correct?

Which of the following Directives are explicitly mentioned in Article 51 (Promotion of international peace and security)? 1. To promote international peace and security. 2. To maintain just and honourable relations between nations. 3. To encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. How many of the above are correct?

Which of the following are broadly categorized as Liberal-Intellectual principles? 1. To secure a uniform civil code for the citizens throughout the country. 2. To separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. 3. To organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines. How many of the above are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the definition of 'State' in Part IV: 1. Article 36 states that the term 'State' in Part IV has exactly the same meaning as in Part III dealing with Fundamental Rights. 2. The obligations of the Directive Principles apply to the Union and State Legislatures, but are not binding on local authorities like municipalities. 3. The Directive Principles are binding on public sector undertakings (PSUs) as they fall under the definition of 'State'. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements comparing Fundamental Rights (FRs) and DPSP: 1. While FRs are negatively worded to prohibit the State from doing certain things, DPSPs are positive directions requiring the State to do certain things. 2. While FRs establish political democracy, DPSPs aim at establishing social and economic democracy. 3. While FRs are generally self-executory, DPSPs are not self-executory and require legislation for their implementation. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the directive 'equal pay for equal work': 1. The directive for 'equal pay for equal work for both men and women' is contained explicitly in Article 39. 2. The Supreme Court has elevated the principle of 'equal pay for equal work' to the status of a fundamental right by reading it along with Article 14. 3. This directive is only applicable to government establishments and not to private industrial establishments. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements regarding the micro-details of the 42nd Amendment additions: 1. Article 39A directs the state to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. 2. Article 43A directs the state to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of all agricultural and industrial establishments. 3. Article 48A directs the state to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country. How many of the above statements are correct?

Regarding the Directives outside Part IV, consider the following statements: 1. These directives are justiciable and can be enforced by the courts unlike the directives in Part IV. 2. They are given equal weightage to the directives contained in Part IV by the judiciary. 3. Article 335 requires the state to take the claims of SCs and STs into consideration while making appointments, but this must be consistent with the maintenance of efficiency of administration. How many of the above statements are correct?

Consider the following statements about the implementation of DPSP: 1. If a state legislature passes a law to implement a DPSP, and that law conflicts with a central law on the Concurrent List, the central law automatically prevails and the state law is void. 2. The President of India is constitutionally bound to reject a constitutional amendment bill if it seeks to alter or dilute any of the Directive Principles. 3. The Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) was established essentially to give effect to the Directive Principle under Article 39. How many of the above statements are correct?
